title: Tokenized SLI Design Patterns and Dashboard Library
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview

Purpose:
This document defines a set of reusable SLI design patterns focused on tokenized inference workloads (latency, cost, cache efficiency, and correctness regressions) and ships a small dashboard library (Grafana/Prometheus) and alert rule examples that platform teams can adopt. The patterns are tuned for Redwood Inference: short/long sequence distributions, model variant fallbacks, KV cache behavior, and cost per token accounting.

Audience:
- Eng-platform/observability engineers building dashboards and alerts
- Runtime and serving teams aligning on SLOs
- SREs on-call for inference endpoints

Scope:
- Prometheus metric names and example queries used in our hosted and dedicated control planes
- Grafana panel designs and example alerting rules (Prometheus Alertmanager format)
- Rollout and validation checklist for applying SLIs to a new model/service
- Incident playbook highlights and retrospective / roadmap recommendations

Terminology
- Tokenized request: a single API request that produces N output tokens.
- Token throughput: tokens generated per second per endpoint.
- Prefix/KV cache hit: reuse of cached KVcache for autoregressive generation.
- Model-variant fallback: automatic switch from preferred model to backup variant when capacity fails or latency exceeds threshold.

Design patterns

1) Tokenized latency SLI (p50/p95/p99 by effective token-length buckets)
- Motivation: latency perception scales with tokens returned; a 200ms p95 for short responses is different from p95 for 2k-token completions.
- Metrics used (Prometheus):
  - redwood_requests_total{endpoint=~"/v1/generate|/v1/chat"}
  - redwood_request_duration_seconds_bucket
  - redwood_request_tokens_returned_total
- Pattern: compute per-request latency percentiles weighted by request count within token-length buckets (0-32, 33-256, 257-1024, 1025+).
- Example queries (Prometheus):
  - "Token bucket p95 (0-32): histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_request_duration_seconds_bucket{token_bucket=\"0-32\"}[5m])) by (le))"
  - "Average tokens per request: sum(rate(redwood_request_tokens_returned_total[5m])) / sum(rate(redwood_requests_total[5m]))"
- Recommended thresholds: p95 <= 250ms (0-32), p95 <= 700ms (33-256), p95 <= 2s (257-1024), p95 <= 4s (1025+). Adjust per-model SLA.

2) Cost-per-token SLI (billable unit economics)
- Motivation: track unit economics for model variants and task types to trigger optimization (quantization, batching) when cost rises.
- Metrics: redwood_tokens_generated_total, redwood_inference_cost_usd_total (estimated by runtime), redwood_inference_batch_size_avg
- Derived metric: cost_per_1000_tokens = (increase in redwood_inference_cost_usd_total / increase in redwood_tokens_generated_total) * 1000.
- Alert rule example: when cost_per_1000_tokens increases >20% over baseline for 6h with traffic > 1k tokens/s.

3) KV cache and prefix reuse SLI
- Motivation: cache reuse reduces CPU/GPU and latency; regressions often come from invalidation logic or model changes.
- Metrics: redwood_kv_cache_hits_total, redwood_kv_cache_misses_total, redwood_kv_cache_size_bytes
- Dashboard panels: hit-rate over time, miss latency distribution, cache eviction rate.
- SLI: weekly hit rate >= 70% for stable chat sessions; alert when drop > 15% absolute vs 24h rolling baseline.

4) Model-fallback correctness and fallback ratio SLI
- Motivation: service-level graceful degradation uses fallback models; we must track quality regressions and fallback ratios to avoid silent correctness loss.
- Metrics: redwood_model_variant_fallback_total, redwood_eval_quality_score_regressions_total (from Canary evals), redwood_requests_total_by_variant
- SLI: fallback_ratio = fallback_requests / total_requests; keep fallback_ratio < 2% under normal load; alert if >5% sustained for 10m or if fallback coincides with quality regressions in eval harness.

Dashboard library (recommended panels and intent)
- Dashboard: Tokenized Latency by Token Bucket
  - Panels: p50/p95/p99 per bucket, requests per bucket, average tokens per request
  - Prometheus expressions: as described above; owner: eng-serving-runtime
  - Alerts: p95 breach per bucket (see thresholds above)
- Dashboard: Cost and Unit Economics
  - Panels: cost_per_1000_tokens (model/route), daily cost trend, batching efficiency (tokens/batch)
  - Owner: eng-platform/costing
- Dashboard: KV Cache Health
  - Panels: hit rate (1m, 5m, 1h), eviction rate, miss latency heatmap, affected routes list
  - Owner: eng-serving-runtime
- Dashboard: Model Variant Stability
  - Panels: fallback ratio, per-variant request share, canary eval pass rate, recent rollouts map
  - Owner: eng-platform/release
- Dashboard JSON snippet (Grafana/Prometheus target example):
  """json
  {
    "title": "p95 latency (0-32 tokens)",
    "expr": "histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_request_duration_seconds_bucket{token_bucket=\"0-32\"}[5m])) by (le))",
    "datasource": "Prometheus"
  }
  """

Alerting rules (examples)
- Alert: tokenized_latency_high_p95
  - Expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_request_duration_seconds_bucket{token_bucket=\"33-256\"}[5m])) by (le)) > 0.7
  - For: 10m
  - Labels: severity=page, team=eng-serving-runtime
  - Annotations: summary="p95 latency high for token bucket 33-256", runbook="/confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/latency-investigation"

- Alert: cost_per_1000_tokens_spike
  - Expr: increase(redwood_inference_cost_usd_total[6h]) / increase(redwood_tokens_generated_total[6h]) * 1000 > (baseline*1.2)
  - For: 30m
  - Labels: severity=pg, team=eng-platform

Implementation checklist (applying patterns to a new route/model)
1. Instrumentation
  - Verify service emits the following metrics: redwood_request_duration_seconds_bucket, redwood_request_tokens_returned_total, redwood_tokens_generated_total, redwood_inference_cost_usd_total, redwood_kv_cache_hits_total, redwood_model_variant_fallback_total.
2. Bucket selection
  - Run a 7-day traffic sample and compute token-length percentiles (p50, p90, p99) then pick bucket boundaries that reflect your traffic shape. Default buckets: 0-32, 33-256, 257-1024, 1025+.
3. Dashboard creation
  - Clone the template panels in the library and point to service labels (route/model tags). Set panel time ranges 15m/1h/24h.
4. Baseline and thresholds
  - Run 48-72h of baseline traffic to compute typical p95s and cost_per_1000_tokens. Store baselines in the dashboard description field.
5. Canary and rollout
  - Add canary evals connected to each deploy. If fallback ratio >2% or canary quality drops, block rollout.

Rollout and validation steps
1. QA environment: enable full instrumentation on QA and create dashboard instances. Validate Prometheus queries and label cardinality.
2. Staged rollout: enable dashboards on canary namespace for 72h, review cost and latency baselines daily.
3. Production enablement: after stable canary, apply alerts to production with a 1-week monitoring window in quiet-alert mode (notifications to a channel, no pages).
4. Full alerting: escalate to pager only after 1 week of stable monitoring and sign-off from owning team.

Incident playbook highlights (for on-call)
- Symptoms and quick checks:
  1. If Tokenized Latency p95 spike: check batch size avg (redwood_inference_batch_size_avg), GPU utilization for nodes serving the model, and prefix cache hit rate.
  2. If cost_per_1000_tokens spiking: check recent deploys, quantization/precision flags, and model size changes.
  3. If fallback ratio rises: check model-serving capacity, scheduler logs, and rollout history.
- Triage steps (ordered):
  1. Identify affected routes/models from dashboard and recent deploys.
  2. If latency: switch traffic to fallback variant (if quality acceptable) or add temporary capacity (scale up dedicated pool).
  3. If cost: disable experimental high-cost feature flags (e.g., full-history-context) and throttle long-response routes.
  4. Post-incident: open a triage ticket, annotate dashboard time ranges, and attach perf/profile artifacts (GPU logs, kernel traces).

Retrospective notes and roadmap recommendations
- Observed recurring root causes from prior incidents: KV cache regression after model topology change; incorrect label cardinality causing Prometheus OOM; cost surprises from unbounded long-response routes.
- Small wins to prioritize: automated token-bucket selector, dashboard templating by route tag, cost anomaly detection job.
- Mid-term roadmap items:
  - 2026 Q2: Ship an automated baseline service that computes per-route baselines and suggests thresholds.
  - 2026 Q3: Integrate canary eval results directly into Grafana with quality glyphs per deploy.
  - 2026 Q4: Add ML-powered cost anomaly detection (owner: eng-platform + research).

Appendices
- Example Prometheus expressions (copy/paste):
  - p95 (0-32): histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_request_duration_seconds_bucket{token_bucket=\"0-32\"}[5m])) by (le))
  - cache hit rate: sum(rate(redwood_kv_cache_hits_total[5m])) / sum(rate(redwood_kv_cache_hits_total[5m]) + rate(redwood_kv_cache_misses_total[5m]))
  - fallback ratio: sum(increase(redwood_model_variant_fallback_total[5m])) / sum(increase(redwood_requests_total[5m]))

- Example labels / metadata conventions for dashboards:
  - team:eng-serving-runtime / team:eng-platform / route:/v1/chat / model:open-xxl / environment:prod
  - Use low-cardinality labels on Prometheus exporters; high-cardinality dimensions should be driven into logs or tracing.

- Runbook links: (create or link before full production alerting)
  - /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/latency-investigation
  - /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/cost-investigation
  - /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/model-fallback-triage

Ownership and maintenance
- Owners: eng-serving-runtime (latency and KV cache panels), eng-platform (cost and unit economics), eng-sre (alerting and escalation policy).
- Maintenance cadence: quarterly review of thresholds after major model rollouts; dashboards get a health check as part of oncall rotation (verify panels show current baselines).
